land.text: Holland, Zeeland and West Friesland: the County of Holland, 'State of the Holy Roman Empire (1091-1581)' (infobox)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has no Holland row before 1260; the page gives 'Established: 11th century'. The dossier starts where the row starts.

land.text: 'From 1433 onward it was part of the Burgundian Netherlands' (County of Holland page)

successors.note: Cliopatria draws Holland inside its 'Duchy of Bavaria' shapes until 1449 and inside Burgundy from 1450. Philip the Good took 'effective control' in 1428 and Jacqueline ceded the inheritance rights in 1432 (County of Hainaut page); the county itself carries on as a title to 1795 (Holland page) but not as a map state.

capitals.name: The Hague
capitals.note: The infobox says 'Capital: The Hague' with no year. The Hainaut page gives 'Capital: Mons' for the county of Hainaut that was joined to Holland by the same counts from 1299; one dot is kept at The Hague.

correction.text: unchanged, for 1260-1298 only: Holland, Zeeland and West Friesland

keyframe_review.note: 8.4 k km2 (bbox 3.4-5.3 E, 51.5-53.2 N): Holland, Zeeland and West Friesland. The page gives no area (only a map 'around 1350'). Floris V 'decided to call himself "Count of Holland and Zeeland, Lord of Friesland"' (1291) and 'It was not until 1289 that Count Floris V was able to bring this long war to an end'. The outline stands for 1260-1298; Hainaut joins in 1299, six years before Cliopatria's 1305 outline (see county-of-holland_1299).

correction.text: Holland and Zeeland with the Hainaut lands round Mons, under the Avesnes counts

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1299-1304: 'From 1299, Hainaut's count Jean II, d'Avesnes, the son of Jean I, was also Count of Holland and Zeeland, through his mother' and the personal-union list 'Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland: 1299-1356'. Cliopatria draws the larger outline (11.6 k km2) only from 1305; the 3.8 k km2 it adds lie at 3.6-4.4 E, 50.0-50.7 N (the Mons country of Hainaut). Only part of Hainaut (the gazetteer's Hainaut province is 11.4 k km2) is in the outline.

11.6 k km2 for 1305-1351: Holland and Zeeland plus the Mons country of Hainaut (the Avesnes union, 1299). No infobox area on either page. Kept as drawn; the Hainaut part has no dossier of its own (see notes).

11.6 k km2, the same outline for 1352-1362. The Wittelsbach hold the counties from 1345 ('In 1345 the emperor ... conferring' Hainaut, Holland, Zeeland and Friesland 'upon his wife, Margaret II of Hainaut'); 'The Hook and Cod Wars were a series of wars and battles in Holland between 1350 and 1490' (Holland page). No border change is dated. Cliopatria's row ends here and the same land then sits inside its Duchy of Bavaria shapes.

correction.text: Holland, Zeeland and the Hainaut lands under the Wittelsbach counts (Bavaria-Straubing), to 1432

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1363-1432, which Cliopatria gives to the Duchy of Bavaria row (92.1 k km2 in 1363-1384 with Brandenburg, 47.7 k km2 in 1385-1449, of which 11.5 k km2 is this land). 'This branch of the Wittelsbach family held Hainaut until 1436'; 'Already in 1428, effective control of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland was acquired by Philip the Good'; 'In 1432 Jacqueline had to cede the inheritance rights of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland to Duke Philip'. The Bavaria-Straubing page names Holland and Hainaut among the lands of the Straubing dukes 'between 1353 and 1432'. Drawn as the 1352 outline.

ledger.note: 1260: Cliopatria's County of Holland begins as Holland, Zeeland and West Friesland. The page gives no 1260 event: 'Established: 11th century', 'State of the Holy Roman Empire (1091-1581)', 'Capital: The Hague'. Date bridged from the Cliopatria row.

1299: the counts of Hainaut become counts of Holland. 'From 1299, Hainaut's count Jean II, d'Avesnes, the son of Jean I, was also Count of Holland and Zeeland, through his mother.' A change of dynasty (the Avesnes) in the same state.

region.text: the Hainaut lands joined to Holland and Zeeland

ledger.note: 1299: Hainaut joins Holland and Zeeland in a personal union ('Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland: 1299-1356'). The year is the page's; the land is Cliopatria's 1305 outline minus its 1260 one, the Mons country of Hainaut (3.8 k km2), not the whole county.

1345: the Wittelsbach become counts. 'In 1345 the emperor further antagonized the lay princes by conferring' Hainaut, Holland, Zeeland and Friesland 'upon his wife, Margaret II of Hainaut.' The County of Hainaut page puts the death of the last Avesnes count in 1347 ('After his grandson William died in 1347, these same lordships went to his sister'); the Louis IV page's 1345 is used. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Holland, Zeeland and the Hainaut lands

ledger.note: 1433: Holland passes to Burgundy. 'From 1433 onward it was part of the Burgundian Netherlands'; 'By the end of the Hook and Cod Wars, Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy, had taken control of Holland.' The Hainaut page has 'Already in 1428, effective control ... was acquired by Philip the Good', 'In 1432 Jacqueline had to cede the inheritance rights ... to Duke Philip' and 'Absorbed into the Burgundian Netherlands: 1432'.

region.text: Holland, Zeeland and the Hainaut lands

ledger.note: 1433: the County of Holland ends as a map state. 'From 1433 onward it was part of the Burgundian Netherlands.' The land goes to the Duchy of Burgundy (Cliopatria's Burgundy 1450 outline includes it).

wars.name: Hook and Cod Wars
belligerents: Hook and Cod factions of the Holland nobility and towns
wars.outcome: 'The Hook and Cod Wars were a series of wars and battles in Holland between 1350 and 1490'; 'By the end of the Hook and Cod Wars, Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy, had taken control of Holland.' No land changed hands between states.
wars.note: A conflict within Holland between factions; the Wittelsbach 'struggled against each other in the so-called Hook and Cod wars' (Hainaut page). Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered; it runs past this dossier's end in 1433.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened. Holland, Zeeland and the Mons lands of Hainaut are drawn as Cliopatria draws them; the border with Utrecht, Guelders and Flanders is approximate throughout.

notes:
HOLLAND. Cliopatria's County of Holland row ends in 1362 and the same land (Holland, Zeeland and the Mons lands of Hainaut, 11.5 k km2) then sits inside its Duchy of Bavaria shapes until 1449 (47.7 k km2 = 36.2 k Bavaria + 11.5 k). This dossier therefore runs to 1433, with one new keyframe for 1363-1432, so that the county is drawn as its own state under the Wittelsbach counts until Burgundy; the duchy-of-bavaria dossier removes the Dutch counties from its outline. The end year 1433 is the Holland page's ('From 1433 onward it was part of the Burgundian Netherlands'); the Hainaut page gives 1432 for the absorption and 1428 for Philip the Good's effective control, and the Duchy of Bavaria page 1436. Cliopatria hands the land to Burgundy only in 1450: the duchy-of-burgundy dossier (eu-10) should start it in 1433.

START. The county dates from the 11th century (infobox); the dossier starts at 1260 where the Cliopatria row starts and pre-1260 Holland is not reviewed.

HAINAUT. The Avesnes counts of Hainaut also held Holland and Zeeland from 1299 and the Wittelsbach held all three from 1345, so Cliopatria's Holland outline from 1305 includes 3.8 k km2 of Hainaut round Mons (3.6-4.4 E, 50.0-50.7 N), not the whole county (the gazetteer's Hainaut province is 11.4 k km2). The County of Hainaut has no Cliopatria row and no dossier: a county-of-hainaut dossier (at least 1260-1433) is needed, and when it exists the Mons lands should move there. Its page was thin on dates: the 'Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland: 1299-1356' union list conflicts with 'This branch of the Wittelsbach family held Hainaut until 1436'.

PAGE BUDGET (1-2): the Holland and Hainaut pages were opened; the Louis IV page (1345 conferral) and the Bavaria-Straubing page (a second page for the 1363 keyframe), both opened for the Bavaria dossier, are cited as a third and fourth. The Holland page gives no area (a map 'around 1350' only), no counts' dates and no Wittelsbach events; the Hainaut page does not name Margaret II of Hainaut as the emperor's wife. Not entered because no page gives a date: the Wittelsbach succession fight of 1345-1354, Jacqueline of Bavaria's war and the Treaty of Delft of 1428, which the Hainaut page mentions only as 'effective control' acquired by Philip the Good. The infobox rulers ('1433-1440: Hugo (first)', '1672-1702: William III (last)') look wrong and no ruler list is given. Counterparts needing dossiers: county-of-hainaut.

Family 'france' is chosen because the colour registry keeps the Netherlands orange as an exception inside that family; the colour agent decides.
